why: phase-446 W6 -- the BOOT-TIME check that a node declares each parameter the way its launch contract's `params:` does, with no upstream counterpart because upstream has no contract to disagree with. The parameter store is sized from that declaration (phase-446 W4), so a name the contract does not declare has no slot and a different type is a value the contract's reader rejects. `Node::declare_parameter` calls it first; a disagreement prints the node, the parameter and the contract, goes through `set_error` (DECLARED_PARAM_MISMATCH, -446) so the entry halts boot, and the parameter is NOT declared. A node whose contract has no `params:` is not checked, nor are the names every node carries. The sibling of `check_declared_depth`, and on `Node` for the same reason: phase-427 W4 deleted `ComponentNode`, where W6 first put it.
